Manipulation, deception, strategy, planning (feats) :

The series «Breaking Bad» has entered the history of cinema and television not only because of its entertainment and exciting plot, but also because of the insightful and subtle manipulations that Walter White, the main character of the series, uses to achieve his goals.

One of the most notable examples of this in the series is the moment with a cigarette and ricin, when Walter White sets up his assistant Jesse against Gustavo Fring. This example is a strong proof of how manipulation can affect other people and that even those who seem naive and weak can become tools in the hands of an experienced and cunning person.
Consider what kinds of manipulations Walter White used to set up Jesse against Gustavo Fring:

The first manipulation that Walter White used was incredibly cunning and sophisticated. He took a cigarette from Jesse and, taking advantage of the temporary turmoil, inserted a small ball of ricin into the filter. Walter knew that ricin was a deadly poison that would kill anyone if consumed in sufficient quantities, and that he could use this knowledge to force Jesse to follow his orders. The scene of Brock's poisoning in the TV series Breaking Bad is a perfect example of how Walter White uses his deception, manipulation, analytical abilities, observation and deduction to achieve his goals.

• Heisenberg wants Jesse to stop working with the group headed by Gustavo Fring, who violated the agreements, leaving Walter without earnings. Jesse, however, doesn't want to hear anything from Walter and continues to work for Fring.

Walter realizes that in order to get Jesse to stop working for Fring, he must prove to him that Gustavo is not an ideal employer. To do this, he decides to use Brock, who was dear to Jesse. Walter hatches a plan according to which he poisoned Brock with cyclodextrin, which leads to Brock's hospitalization. White then makes Jesse believe that Fring poisoned Brock to frame Walter in Jesse's eyes. Heisenberg uses his powers of observation and analytical ability to conduct an actual analysis of how Brock was poisoned and conclude that it was cyclodextrin. He also uses his deduction skills to come up with a plan to poison Brock and show Jesse that only Fring could have done it.
Walter also uses his deception and manipulation skills to get Jesse to believe his story and stop working for Fring. Walter even convinces Jesse that Brock is dead, which turns out to be a lie.
This scene demonstrates how sophisticated Walter White is in his actions and how easily he can use manipulation and deception to achieve his goals.

This time Walter finds himself in a very dangerous situation. He realizes that Mike, Fring's hired killer, may kill him and Jesse in order to keep Gustavo's secret and ensure his safety. And when Mike already wanted to eliminate Walter for incomprehensible actions and asks: «What the hell just happened.» Walter gives Gale's address, thereby informing Mike of his plan and saying that Gustavo needs them, hinting at Gale's imminent death. This scene shows very well how White uses his skills of deception, manipulation, planning, strategy and persuasion to find a way out of a dangerous situation and achieve his goals.

Another manipulation that Walter White used to turn Jesse against Gustavo Fring was related to Mike Ehrmantraut. Walter knew that Mike respected him only for his professionalism, but he never trusted him enough to give him power on an equal footing. Walter used this to convince Jesse that Mike is an enemy, not a friend. Walter told Jesse that Mike was going to sell them both to Gustavo Fring to save his life, and that they had to act quickly to thwart his plans. This helped Walter make Jesse realize that Mike was against him, not for him, and made Jesse join his ideas.

To complete the manipulation, Walter decided to kill Mike to finally convince Jesse that he was the best choice for him. Walter understood that Mike had always been a problem, and eliminating him would help Jesse establish himself in his place, leaving Walter free to act in his affairs. Unfortunately, this time the manipulation did not go smoothly, and Mike's murder led to the fact that Walter and Jesse's relationship broke up, and this led to tragedies.

In conclusion, we can say that Walter White was an expert at manipulating other people. His ability to use manipulation for his own purposes was one of the key factors in his success in the fight against Gustavo Fring. Walter showed that even innocent people like Jesse can become tools in the hands of more experienced and cunning people, and that you should always remember this before sharing your firm beliefs with someone.
